text: The three document reads of the legal key are consumed on the rwb-document base as GET /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents (id, caseId, documentType, writeOnce), GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/fields (fieldName and the masked fieldValue) and GET /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/document-checklist (the itemCode list of the case type), each one hop with the 2 s client budget, a fake, and a failed read mapped to run status TOOL_UNAVAILABLE with the reason naming the read; the by-case legal-action read of rwb-litigation is consumed as a by-case read of the open action with id, actionType and status.
why: RWB-P5-E2025-CON and the rwb-litigation contract are named as the owners of the documents, the fields, the checklist and the legal action, and no source publishes the paths below their bases or the member names, so the app story, the consumed rows and the fakes need one stated shape.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-030 sections 4, 11, 12 and 13; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.9; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1 and T5.2; context pack P10 (base, one hop, 2 s, DP-01 and DP-11)
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-document and rwb-litigation owners in the baseline review of RWB-P10-E2030-CON.
impact: If P5 or S4 publishes another path or another member, one consumed row, one adapter and one fixture change per read; no schema, event or workflow change.

text: A shadow run of the legal key is started by the evaluation harness inside rwb-agent and not by an operation of its own: one AgentRunWorkflow execution per case and evaluation run, with the evaluation run ID on the run row, and no run-start operation is consumed by a screen.
why: The legacy flow starts the runs from the evaluation of POST /admin/agent-evaluations and no source names a run-start operation, so the app story needs one stated trigger for its 50 runs.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-030 section 4 steps 1 to 5 and section 13 (build steps); FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.5; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T-A.1; context pack P10 (AgentRunWorkflow, queue rwb-agent)
confirm: Solution architect with the P10 owner before the app story starts.
impact: If a run-start operation is needed for a screen, one provided row, its rights and its test case are added to RWB-P10-E2030-CON; the workflow and the run rows do not change.

text: The minimum scored sample of 50, the promotion check list and the 60-second timeout are read at load time as parameter values of rwb-case through GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters, and the six lists are read as reference data through GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}; the parameter codes and the list codes are fixed with the rwb-case owner, and no value is written in code.
why: The legacy story states the minimum sample and the promotion conditions as policy values and writes no business value in code, and the parameter and list codes are not named by any source, so the refusals of AC7 and AC8 and the six LOV reads need one stated source.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-030 sections 3, 7, 8 and 13; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.5.3.1 and A2.9.3.1; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.2; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-06 and DP-07
applied_in: RWB-P10-E2030-APP 2, 3, 8 (BR6, BR9), 12.2 and AC7, AC8; RWB-P10-E2030-CON 12.2 and AC4, AC5
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-case owner in the baseline review of RWB-P10-E2030-CON.
impact: If a code differs, one consumed row and one fixture change; the checks and their messages are unaffected.

text: The completion event of the legal key is EV-28 AgentRunCompleted only, and its payload carries the run facts - run ID, agent code, agent version, prompt version, case ID, autonomy mode, trigger event, status, fallback, confidence, latency, tokens, cost and run-at - with no item, no document ID, no defect reason and no personal field; the pack and the completeness list stay in agent_run.output and are returned by no user-facing operation.
why: The catalogue names EV-28 with five members and the legacy story names no second event, while AC1 requires that no user-facing endpoint returns the pack, so the payload boundary and the absence of a pack event need one statement.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-030 sections 7 (AC1), 12 and 17; Recovery Workbench Event and Messaging Design v4 (EV-28 row); context pack P10 (EV-28 and the no-PII rule)
applied_in: RWB-P10-E2030-APP 12.3 and AC1; RWB-P10-E2030-CON 12.3 and AC6
confirm: Data steward and the solution architect in the baseline review.
impact: If a consumer needs a pack fact, the topic is extended additively within major version 1 after the data-steward review; no table changes.

text: The seven operations of the legal key are reached through one gateway-bff composite route of one hop that preserves the JSON and CSV media types and passes a refusal through unchanged; its name and path are fixed by RWB-PLT-N001-CON and not by this story.
why: DP-19 requires the composite route and no source names it, so the app story's screens and its access test need one stated route without inventing a path.
read: Template and Rules R5.5 DP-19; context pack P10 (gateway-bff and the edge rule); Arch v5 slide 8
applied_in: RWB-P10-E2030-APP 12.1, 15 and TC-E2-030-10; RWB-P10-E2030-CON 12.8 and AC7
confirm: Platform library owner in the baseline review of RWB-P10-E2030-CON.
impact: If the route name or path differs, one row and one stub change; no behaviour changes.

text: The pack, the completeness list and the defect reasons are stored in agent_run.output only: they are published on no topic, returned by no user-facing operation, and read back through GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/agent-runs/{runId} under Platform administration R with the scope applied.
why: The legacy story forbids showing the pack and gives no reader for it, so the contract must state where the pack lives and who reads it without inventing a screen.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-030 sections 7 (AC1), 12 and 15; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1 (DF-AGT-049) and T-A.2 API-P10-001; context pack P10 (ownership rows)
applied_in: RWB-P10-E2030-CON 12.1, 12.3, 12.7 and AC2, AC6; RWB-P10-E2030-APP 12.3 and AC1
confirm: Data steward and the P10 owner in the baseline review.
impact: If a reader is added, one provided row and its rights are added; no event and no table change.

text: The consumed boundary of the contract is the three document reads on the rwb-document base, the by-case legal-action read of rwb-litigation and the case read of rwb-case, with the member names of ASM-B2-P10-004-1 and a 2 s client budget each; the checklist items are the itemCode values of the P5 checklist read, and the type of documentIds is an array of strings.
why: The contract needs one boundary shape for the app story and the Epic 5 pack story, and no source publishes the paths, the member names or the pack member types.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-030 sections 11 and 12; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1 and T5.2; API Specification v4 AgentRun; context pack P10 (one hop, 2 s, DP-01, DP-11)
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-document, rwb-litigation and rwb-case owners before the baseline is tagged.
impact: A path or member change is one row, one adapter and one fixture per read; the pack shape is unaffected unless itemCode changes, which is a breaking change to legal-pack-v1.

text: The policy payload of the legal key is the baseline AgentConfigVersion request narrowed with six additive members - evaluationRunId, promotionConditions, allowedTools, outputSchemaRef, timeoutSeconds and the mode value SHADOW or L1 with its reviewDate - and no member of the baseline is removed or retyped.
why: AC3, AC7 and AC8 need the evaluation run ID, the conditions, the review date and the 60-second timeout on the version, and the baseline resource names only some of them.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-030 sections 3, 7 and 12; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.6.3.2; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1 DF-AGT-006, DF-AGT-007, DF-AGT-012, DF-AGT-016, DF-AGT-017 and DF-AGT-018; API Specification v4 AgentConfigVersion
applied_in: RWB-P10-E2030-CON 11, 12.1 and AC4; RWB-P10-E2030-APP 12.1 and AC3, AC8
confirm: Solution architect with the P10 owner and the P7 owner for the approval rule.
impact: An additive member is a schema change inside major version 1; removing or retyping one is a breaking change reviewed with the owner of the baseline.

text: The score row of the legal key is the baseline AgentEvaluation with the checklist itemCode as its labelKey, the sample size in sampleSize and the agreement rate in agreementRate at four decimals (DF-AGT-089, DF-AGT-090, DF-AGT-094); a case that did not run is listed with its failure type and is excluded from the scored sample, which the report states as 49.
why: AC2 and AC6 need 0.9200 on 46 of 50 and 49 scored cases, and no source fixes the label key or the treatment of a not-run case in the row.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-030 sections 7 (AC2, AC6) and 8 (BR5); TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1 DF-AGT-089 to DF-AGT-094 and T3.2 LOV-AGENT-RUN; API Specification v4 AgentEvaluation and AgentEvaluationReport
applied_in: RWB-P10-E2030-CON 11, 12.1 and AC5; RWB-P10-E2030-APP 12.1 and AC2, AC6
confirm: Solution architect with the P10 owner and the data steward.
impact: A different label key changes the score rows and the report only; no event and no table change.

text: The run start of the legal key is fixed as POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/agent-runs with agent, caseId, evaluationRunId and the idempotency key, answering 202 with an AgentRun, and the run read stays GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/agent-runs/{runId} with the six members of API-P10-001 plus autonomyMode, guardrailResult, output and evaluationRunId.
why: The sources name the run read on Arch v5 slide 16 and no start operation, and the app story and the harness need one start shape to build and test against.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-030 sections 4 and 12; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T-A.1 API-P10-001 and T3.1; Arch v5 slide 16; context pack P10 (base /api/recovery/agent/v1)
confirm: Solution architect and the P10 owner in the baseline review.
impact: If the platform fixes another start path, one provided row, its rights and one test case change; the run rows, the workflow and the event do not change.

text: The gateway-bff route in front of the legal operations is one composite route of one hop that preserves the JSON and CSV media types and passes a refusal through unchanged; its name, its path and the rwb-agent service identity are the platform's and are fixed with RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the deployment story, not by this contract.
why: DP-19 requires the route for every screen call, and no source names the route or the service login, so the contract must state the boundary without inventing either value.
